origin.description: Tune the ICU regular-expression matcher used by the regex search functions.
origin.usage: stri_opts_regex(case_insensitive, comments, dotall, dot_all = dotall, literal, multiline, multi_line = multiline, unix_lines, uword, error_on_unknown_escapes, time_limit = 0L, stack_limit = 0L)

arguments.name: case_insensitive
arguments.text: Logical. Case-insensitive matching, the same idea as the (?i) flag.

arguments.name: comments
arguments.text: Logical. Allow white space and comments in the pattern, as with (?x).

arguments.name: dotall
arguments.text: Logical. If TRUE, "." matches line terminators. If FALSE, "." stops at a line end. This is (?s).

arguments.name: dot_all
arguments.text: Alias of dotall. The stored name is dotall.

arguments.name: literal
arguments.text: Logical. If TRUE, the pattern is a literal string. Fixed search is the usual tool for that.

arguments.name: multiline
arguments.text: Logical. If TRUE, ^ and $ also match at line breaks. If FALSE, they match only the ends of the input. This is (?m).

arguments.name: multi_line
arguments.text: Alias of multiline. The stored name is multiline.

arguments.name: unix_lines
arguments.text: Logical. If TRUE, only U+000A is a line ending for ".", ^, and $.

arguments.name: uword
arguments.text: Logical. If TRUE, word boundaries follow Unicode TR 29, as with (?w). Those boundaries differ from traditional regex words.

arguments.name: error_on_unknown_escapes
arguments.text: Logical. If TRUE, a backslash before an ASCII letter with no special meaning is an error. If FALSE, that letter stands for itself.

arguments.name: time_limit
arguments.text: Integer. Approximate match time limit in milliseconds. 0 means no limit. The documented default is 0.

arguments.name: stack_limit
arguments.text: Integer. Maximum backtracking-stack size in bytes. 0 means no limit. The documented default is 0.

origin.details: Some of the same switches can be written inside a pattern with ICU flags such as (?i). The list stores only supplied settings. stack_limit is placed before time_limit. dotall and multiline win over their aliases.
origin.value: A named list. Missing settings stay at the matcher defaults. NULL drops that name.

translation.description: Regex matcher settings as a dict of the values that were passed.
translation.usage: stri_opts_regex(case_insensitive, comments, dotall, dot_all, literal, multiline, multi_line, unix_lines, uword, error_on_unknown_escapes, time_limit=0, stack_limit=0)

arguments.name: case_insensitive
arguments.text: Logical. Case-insensitive matching.

arguments.name: comments
arguments.text: Logical. Allow white space and comments in the pattern.

arguments.name: dotall
arguments.text: Logical. True lets "." match line terminators.

arguments.name: dot_all
arguments.text: Alias stored as dotall. Ignored when dotall is also passed, including when dotall is None.

arguments.name: literal
arguments.text: Logical. True treats the whole pattern as literal text.

arguments.name: multiline
arguments.text: Logical. True lets ^ and $ match at line breaks.

arguments.name: multi_line
arguments.text: Alias stored as multiline. Ignored when multiline is also passed.

arguments.name: unix_lines
arguments.text: Logical. True recognizes only U+000A as a line ending.

arguments.name: uword
arguments.text: Logical. True uses Unicode TR 29 word boundaries.

arguments.name: error_on_unknown_escapes
arguments.text: Logical. True rejects a backslash before an unknown ASCII letter.

arguments.name: time_limit
arguments.text: Integer milliseconds for a match. 0 means no limit. Omit it to leave the setting out.

arguments.name: stack_limit
arguments.text: Integer byte limit for the backtracking stack. 0 means no limit. Omit it to leave the setting out.

translation.details: The recorded order is case_insensitive, comments, literal, unix_lines, uword, error_on_unknown_escapes, stack_limit, time_limit, dotall, multiline. The prefix dot is ambiguous. A longer list warns and keeps the first element. An empty list raises replacement has length zero.
translation.value: A dict of supplied settings. True and False stand for TRUE and FALSE. None stands for NULL and is not stored.
